To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the large N limit of the N =2 SUSY gauge theory with gauge group S U ( N ) is a non-critical string theory in four dimensions, that the critical points of this string theory correspond to multicritical points of the N = 2 SUSY gauge theories, and that the amplitudes in these non-critical strings can be calculated in the large N limit by a generalization of the matrix model approach.

the exact amplitudes of the large N expansion of the N = 2 supersymmetric Yang Mills theory with gauge group $SU(N)$ break down at the singularities on the Coulomb branch, but that by taking $N\to \infty$ and approaching the singular points in a correlated way the observables of this field theory have a finite limit that is given by the amplitudes of a non-critical string theory in 4 dimensions.

the large N expansion of four-dimensional non-supersymmetric Yang–Milles theory with gauge group U( N ) breaks down at singularities and that the large N limit of the theory is described by non-critical string theory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the large N behaviour of supersymmetric Yang–Mil theory.
the study of the non-critical string duals to N =2 supersymetric gauge theories in the large N limit.
the study of non-critical string theory in four dimensions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the exact amplitudes of the N =2 SYM theory with gauge group U( N ) in four dimensions, in the planar limit, are equal to the amplitudes of a string theory in four dimensions, with a string coupling g s ∼ N 0, in the limit of large N and small string coupling.
the large N expansion of supersymmetric gauge theories is a powerful tool to study non-critical strings.

the large N expansion of the N =2 supersymmetry Yang–Mills theories breaks down at singularities in the moduli space of these theories, and the singularities are resolved in a non-perturbative way by the non-critical string theory dual to these Yang–Mills field theories.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in four-dimensional noncritical string theories, the amplitudes are given by the exact amplitudes of the corresponding matrix model.
the non-critical string is an exact description for the N →∞ limit of a certain family of four-dimensional field theories with a large number of colours.
the N =2 supersymmetry of the gauge theory is spontaneously broken by the singularities of the theory, and the string amplitudes we find are amplitudes in a non-supersymmetric string theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the non-critical strings that arise in the large N expansion of four-dimensional supersymmetric gauge theories are not the usual non-critical strings of string theory, but rather are new objects that have not been previously considered in string theory.
the large N limit of N =2 SYM is a non-critical string theory with an infinite number of degrees of freedom.
, in the large N limit, non-critical strings can be described by field theories in four dimensions.
